items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The final file isn't shown, only a 6176-byte jump_analyzer.py with analyze_jump_video(). The summary mentions fixed areas like x ∈ [250,750] and Cy baselines, so I can't confirm the naming or comments are clear. Partial view only.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: One function, analyze_jump_video, seems to hold tracking, peak finding and contact logic, instead of separate measurement and detection functions. /app/scratch/ (about 15 debug scripts plus frame PNGs) and __pycache__ were left in /app.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: There are many fixed pixel constants: hurdle region x 250–750, ground-baseline and ymax heuristics. An early version printed takeoff=land=97, so fallbacks hide failures without raising an error. I see no clear sign of cap.isOpened() or file checks.

items.name: Robust to bad inputs and missing detections
items.name_zh: 异常输入与检测失败的处理
items.evidence: The thresholds are absolute pixel values tuned on the example video ("x ∈ [250, 750]", ground ymax). The hidden test video failed. An earlier version produced 97/97 without complaint. No clear non-zero exit when there is no jump or the video won't open.

items.name: Output contract honoured
items.evidence: Reads argv[1] (`jump_analyzer.py /app/example_video.mp4`) and writes /app/output.toml with exactly the two integer fields. Frame numbering isn't stated: it is probably 0-based, while the reference counts from 1.
